title: Wounded Chiefs, Negotiation, and the Gazdi Transition

blocks.text: By the close of the fighting, many chiefs were wounded, and the cost of the battle is measured through the battered bodies of leading sardars. Jassa Singh received two grievous wounds, making his suffering emblematic of the price paid by the Khalsa in a fight triggered by treachery.

Sadiq Beg now falls back on negotiation and tries to repair the breach through envoys, compensation, and renewed promises of settlement. The Singhs hear the offer, but their answer is stern: delay in ransom would bring renewed plunder, because bad faith has already been proved in the field.

This settlement talk also becomes a transition into the next political sequence. The page closes the betrayal episode while opening the wider Gazdi narrative, where arrogance, court intrigue, and new alignments will again shape the struggle.
